subject: [PATCH] mm/memory: refuse to map page cache folios that are not uptodate

reviews.author: Pedro Falcato
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about the patch's approach, suggesting that it may become too error-prone if filesystems can randomly clear the uptodate flag. Proposed addressing this problem first.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 11:32:44AM +0000, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> On Sat, Nov 07, 2026 at 07:17:52PM +0100, David Hildenbrand (Arm) wrote:
> > > - [Medium] mm: missing folio_test_uptodate() recheck in
> > >   do_shared_fault() mkwrite path
> > 
> > Kiryl, can you look into that?
> 
> Yeah, that's legit. Will fix in v2.

Related: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/as-fqjiGj5T5NLOe@casper.infradead.org/

At some point, if filesystems can randomly clear uptodate as a way to signal
writeback failure (even without the folio lock!!), these kinds of checks can
become a bit too error prone.

Perhaps we need to address this problem first?

-- 
Pedro

reviews.author: David Hildenbrand (Arm)
reviews.summary: Asked for clarification on whether the patch should use WARN or not, and questioned the legitimacy of mapping a folio without the uptodate flag set.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau
reviews.summary: Confirmed that the patch is a good idea and will fix it in v2, but also provided additional information about filesystems holding the folio lock.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 11:37:42AM +0000, Pedro Falcato wrote:
> On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 11:32:44AM +0000, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:
> > On Sat, Nov 07, 2026 at 07:17:52PM +0100, David Hildenbrand (Arm) wrote:

> > > >   do_shared_fault() mkwrite path
> > > 
> > > Kiryl, can you look into that?
> > 
> > Yeah, that's legit. Will fix in v2.
> 
> Related: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/as-fqjiGj5T5NLOe@casper.infradead.org/
> 
> At some point, if filesystems can randomly clear uptodate as a way to signal
> writeback failure (even without the folio lock!!), these kinds of checks can
> become a bit too error prone.
> 
> Perhaps we need to address this problem first?

The clearers Sashiko pointed at (ext4, ecryptfs, ntfs) hold the folio
lock. Which one does it without?

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Pedro Falcato
reviews.summary: Corrected Kiryl's statement about filesystems holding the folio lock, and clarified that they are safe from that angle.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 11:58:18AM +0000, Kiryl Shutsemau wrote:

> > 
> > At some point, if filesystems can randomly clear uptodate as a way to signal
> > writeback failure (even without the folio lock!!), these kinds of checks can
> > become a bit too error prone.
> > 
> > Perhaps we need to address this problem first?
> 
> The clearers Sashiko pointed at (ext4, ecryptfs, ntfs) hold the folio
> lock. Which one does it without?

You seem to be correct, from a quick look I can't find anyone doing this
without the folio lock. So it seems we're safe from that angle.

So the only thing we _cannot_ do is assert this on e.g an unmap (since we
stop holding the folio lock).

-- 
Pedro

2026-11-09.patch_summary: Patch to refuse mapping page cache folios that are not uptodate, sparking a discussion about the implications of filesystems clearing the uptodate flag.
